content:
{'translation': "Not everyone knows this (and I won't pretend I did), but Apple actually publishes extremely detailed dimensional drawings for dozens of its devices to help accessory manufacturers design compatible products. Here are the details."}

{'translation': 'Apple hardware, laid bare'}

{'translation': "For nearly three decades, Jason Kottke has been one of my primary sources of interesting things on the internet (and beyond), and I'm sure there's a great deal I would never have discovered without him."}

{'translation': 'A few days ago, he posted a link to the "Dimensional Drawings" section of the accessories area on Apple\'s developer site.'}

{'translation': "In short, it's a repository of highly detailed technical drawings, currently covering 96 devices, including the new iPhone 18 Pro, Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Series 12, and AirPods 5."}

{'translation': 'The list also includes products like MacBook Neo and the Siri Remote, as well as accessories such as AirTag, AirPods charging cases, and ZEISS Optical Inserts for Apple Vision Pro.'}

{'translation': 'Each document contains precise measurements of everything from overall device dimensions and curves to buttons, cameras, sensors, speakers and ports, along with detailed "keepout zone" markings showing where specific materials must not be placed.'}

{'translation': "Although these documents are primarily intended for accessory manufacturers, anyone with even a passing interest in hardware, industrial design, or simply the meticulous nature of Apple's products should find them worth a look."}

{'translation': "To view Apple's dimensional drawings, follow this link. And if you're not already following kottke.org, you should start now."}
